test_title: PYST 2: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - Quant (Held On 25 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A shopkeeper lists a jacket for ₹2000. He offers a discount of 15% on the list price. What additional discount (on the reduced price) must he offer to bring the final price down to ₹1360?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

After 15% discount → price = 2000 × 0.85 = 1700

Need final = 1360

Reduction = 1700 − 1360 = 340

Required % = (340 ÷ 1700) × 100 = 20%

**∴ Answer = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked price = 2000

First discount = 15%

Final price = 1360

**Formula:**

Successive discount formula

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after first discount = 2000 − (15% of 2000)

⇒ = 2000 − 300 = 1700

⇒ Let second discount = x%

⇒ Final price = 1700 × (1 − x ÷ 100)

⇒ 1700 × (1 − x ÷ 100) = 1360

⇒ 1 − x ÷ 100 = 1360 ÷ 1700 = 0.8

⇒ x ÷ 100 = 0.2

⇒ x = 20%

**∴ Final Answer: 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Successive Discount:** Net factor = (1 − d1) × (1 − d2)

**Quick Trick:** Always convert % to multiplier

**Reverse Calculation:** Work backward from final price

**Exam Tip:** Use ratio instead of equation when possible
